stories.title: 'Rainbow-on-a-chip' could help unlock 6G networks and precision timing for quantum technologies
stories.desc: Loughborough University physicists and an international team have demonstrated that a grain-of-rice-sized microchip can be used to produce a spectrum of precisely spaced frequencies of light, which is then converted into multiple high-frequency electromagnetic signals known as millimeter waves.

stories.title: Laser-cut aluminum foil could replace costly terahertz polarizers
stories.desc: When physicists at the ARC Centre for Transformative Meta-Optical Systems (TMOS) needed a key component for their terahertz experiments, they ran into a frustrating problem—they needed tiny optical devices, known as wire-grid polarizers, but these cost thousands of dollars each.
